html:
The Podgorica Assembly was a gathering that voted on 26 November 1918 to depose King Nicholas I and unite Montenegro with Serbia, days before the founding of the Yugoslav kingdom.

Its delegates were chosen in hurried elections while Serbian troops held the country. Supporters of union printed their lists on white paper, opponents on green, which gave the two camps their names. The Greens rose in the Christmas Uprising of January 1919 and fought a guerrilla war for years. The vote ended Montenegro as a state until 2006, and the quarrel between those who see Montenegrins as Serbs and those who do not still marks its politics.
sum: The Podgorica Assembly was a gathering that voted on 26 November 1918 to depose King Nicholas I and unite Montenegro with Serbia, days before the founding of the Yugoslav kingdom.
